City council approves new budget for public transport

2 March 2026

The city council voted 31 to 14 on Monday to approve a 120 million euro budget for public transport, according to the official meeting minutes published on the council website.

"This budget lets us replace a third of the bus fleet by 2028," said Deputy Mayor Petar Georgiev in a statement after the vote. Opposition councillor Elena Dimitrova told reporters that the plan underfunds tram maintenance.

The figures were published by the National Statistical Institute and the full document is available on the council portal. Transport unions said they would study the details before commenting.

The council estimates that ridership grew 8% last year. Independent analysts at the university transport institute said the projection was plausible but depended on fuel prices, which have been volatile.

The budget now goes to the regional governor, who has 14 days to sign it or return it to the council with objections, a spokesperson for the governor's office said.
